turns.prompt_text: I take pictures of a lot of text, often my Google pixel 9 does not focus correctly and I don't get sentences
turns.response_html:
That is a known quirk with modern flagship phones, including the Pixel 9. Because these devices use physically larger camera sensors with a wider aperture to capture more light, they have a naturally narrow depth of field.

When you get close to a flat page of text, the center of the image will be sharp, but the physics of the lens causes the outer edges and corners of the document to blur or fall out of focus.

Here are the best ways to bypass this and get crisp, readable text every time:

1. The "2x Zoom and Back Up" Trick

Instead of holding your phone close to the document, back up about a foot or two and switch the camera to 2x zoom.

  • Why it works: By physically moving the phone further away, you flatten the depth of field, bringing the entire page into the same focal plane. The 2x high-res crop ensures you don't lose any detail.

2. Lock the Focus Manually

Google's autofocus can sometimes hunt or get confused by the high contrast of text patterns.

  • Tap the specific sentence or area you want to read on your viewfinder screen.
  • To lock it completely so it doesn't shift when you move slightly, press and hold the screen until the focus ring turns yellow and displays a lock icon.

3. Check for Macro Focus Interference

If you have a base Pixel 9, or a Pro model with Macro Focus set to "Auto," the phone might be rapidly switching to the ultra-wide lens when it thinks you're too close. This can cause the lens to jitter or fail to lock focus on text.

  • Try pulling back slightly until the macro icon (the little flower) disappears, or force it off in your camera quick settings to keep the main lens stable.

4. Wipe the Laser Autofocus Sensor

The Pixel 9 relies heavily on a small laser autofocus sensor located in the camera bar next to the lenses.

  • If a stray fingerprint, smudge, or dust caught inside a phone case cutout blocks that sensor, the camera will constantly struggle to measure distance. Give the entire camera bar a quick wipe with a soft cloth.
